content.text: Section 20 satisfies every preferred element, and Section 21.3 makes indemnification obligations an Excluded Claim (uncapped — better for us than the fallback 3× super-cap). No redline needed.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. § 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates (definition at § 1.1) against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP, with no Customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs. § 20.2 extends the same defence and indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. § 20.4 supplies the standard procedure — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation (at the indemnifying Party's expense) and control of the defence — plus a settlement-consent protection for us. § 20.3 keeps our reciprocal indemnity narrow: unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. § 20.5 also delivers the fallback procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder. The fallback 3× annual fees super-cap is unnecessary and would be worse for us: § 21.3 lists indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the § 21.1 cap entirely. No redline.
